title: Review: Newton's second law; Momentum and its conservation; Impulse and force–time graphs; Work done; Kinetic and potential energy; conservation; Work–energy theorem and dissipative forces; Power and efficiency
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Eduqas A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: E03-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; E03-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; E02-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; D10-1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: D03-1#N.2, D09-1#N.10a, D10-1#N.12, E01-1#N.9b, E02-1#N.12, E03-1#N.15, E04-1#N.11, D09-1#N.2, E01-1#N.5, E02-1#N.4a, E04-1#N.6b, D09-1#N.7. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Power
items.clue: Rate of doing work, or rate of energy transfer.

items.label: Watt
items.clue: Unit equal to one joule transferred each second.

items.label: Kinetic energy
items.clue: What an object has because it is moving; four times larger at double the speed.

items.label: Impulse
items.clue: Vector in N s pointing along the resultant force, not necessarily along the motion.

questions.stem: A crate slides to the left across a level floor with negligible friction. At one instant, two students push on it horizontally: one pushes to the left with a force of 20 N, and the other pushes to the right with a force of 30 N. Which statement about the crate at this instant is correct?

options.text: Its speed is increasing, as there is a net force exerted on it.
Its acceleration is to the left, the direction it is moving.
Its speed is decreasing, as its acceleration is to the right.
Its speed is constant, as the net force exerted on it is constant.

questions.stem: A 0.50 kg trolley moving at 5.0 m s⁻¹ collides with a 3.0 kg trolley at rest on a level track with negligible friction. After the collision, the 0.50 kg trolley moves backwards at 1.0 m s⁻¹ and the 3.0 kg trolley moves forwards at 1.0 m s⁻¹. How much of the system's kinetic energy is transformed into other forms of energy?

Two identical 0.50 kg gliders on an air track each move at 2.0 m s⁻¹ towards an obstacle. Glider 1 hits a steel buffer and bounces straight back at 2.0 m s⁻¹; the contact lasts 0.010 s. Glider 2 hits a foam pad and stops; the contact lasts 0.040 s. How many times larger is the average force on glider 1 than the average force on glider 2?

options.text: 1, as both gliders arrive with the same speed

questions.stem: A student carries a bag of weight 15 N up a flight of stairs at constant velocity. The bag moves 4.0 m horizontally and rises 3.0 m, so it travels 5.0 m along the stairs. How much work does the student's upward force do on the bag?

options.text: 60 J, the upward force multiplied by the horizontal distance.
45 J, the upward force multiplied by the height gained.
75 J, the upward force multiplied by the distance along the stairs.
Zero, as the bag moves at constant velocity, so no work is done on it.

questions.explanation: The force is vertical and the displacement is 5.0 m at an angle θ to it, with cos θ = 3.0/5.0. Work = 15 × 5.0 × 0.60 = 45 J: the force times the 3.0 m rise.

questions.stem: Three identical stones are thrown from the top of a sea cliff with the same speed: one straight up, one horizontally and one straight down. Air resistance is negligible. Which stone hits the sea with the greatest speed?

options.text: The one thrown straight down, as its velocity starts in the direction of gravity.
The one thrown upwards, as it falls back from a greater height than the others.
The one thrown horizontally, as it keeps its horizontal speed while gaining vertical speed.
All land at equal speeds: same starting kinetic energy, same drop in height.

questions.explanation: Initial kinetic energy + potential energy lost = final kinetic energy, and both terms are equal for all three stones. The speeds are equal; only the directions and times of flight differ.

questions.stem: Motor A raises a 200 N load through 3.0 m in 6.0 s. Motor B raises a 100 N load through 6.0 m in 4.0 s. Both lift at constant speed. Which statement is correct?

options.text: A develops more power, as it lifts the heavier load.
B does more work, as it lifts its load twice as high.
Both do equal work, and B develops more power.
Both develop equal power, as they do equal work.

questions.explanation: Each does 600 J (200 × 3.0 and 100 × 6.0). B does it in less time: 600 ÷ 4.0 = 150 W against 600 ÷ 6.0 = 100 W.

questions.stem: A block on a level, frictionless surface is sped up by a constant horizontal force. The work needed to speed the block up from rest to speed v is W. How many times W is needed to speed the block up from v to 3v?

A cricket ball of mass m moving horizontally with speed v is struck by a bat. It leaves the bat moving horizontally with speed 3v/2 in the opposite direction. Taking the ball's initial direction of motion as positive, what is the change in the ball's momentum?
A worker uses a rope to lower a box straight down at constant speed. Which statement about the work done on the box during the descent is correct?

options.text: The tension does positive work and gravity does negative work on the box.
The tension does negative work and gravity does positive work.
The tension and gravity both do positive work on the box as it moves.
Neither force does any work, as the box's speed does not change.

questions.stem: Object A has mass m and moves at speed 2v. Object B has mass 2m and moves at speed v. What is the kinetic energy of object A divided by the kinetic energy of object B?

options.text: ½

questions.explanation: A: ½m(2v)² = 2mv². B: ½(2m)v² = mv². So A has twice B's kinetic energy: doubling the speed multiplies it by 4, doubling the mass only by 2.

questions.stem: A skier of mass 60 kg starts from rest at the top of a slope and descends through a vertical height of 20 m. At the bottom her speed is 16 m s⁻¹. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the total work done on the skier by friction and air resistance during the descent?

Two blocks, of masses 1.0 kg and 4.0 kg, are held at rest on a horizontal surface with negligible friction, with a compressed spring between them. When they are released, the 1.0 kg block moves off at 2.0 m s⁻¹. Which statement about the 4.0 kg block is correct?

options.text: It moves off at 2.0 m s⁻¹, in the opposite direction.
It moves off at 0.50 m s⁻¹, in the opposite direction.
It moves off at 8.0 m s⁻¹, in the opposite direction.
It stays at rest, as the total momentum must stay zero.

questions.explanation: Total momentum starts at zero and stays zero: 4.0 × v = 1.0 × 2.0, so v = 0.50 m s⁻¹, opposite to the 1.0 kg block.
